questions.sec: PBC: definition, AMA/PDHE2, hepatic vs cholestatic note, prevalence, associations, algorithm and presentation
questions.q: Fill up (opening line of the chapter): Primary Biliary Cirrhosis / Primary Biliary Cholangitis is the cardinal example of ______ cholestasis.
questions.exp: The chapter opens: 'Cardinal example of intrahepatic cholestasis.' (Book p1020)

questions.sec: PBC: definition, AMA/PDHE2, hepatic vs cholestatic note, prevalence, associations, algorithm and presentation
questions.q: Judge the two statements from the printed definition of PBC: I It is an autoimmune disease with chronic progressive non-suppurative inflammatory destruction. II The target is the large extrahepatic bile ducts.
questions.exp: Definition: autoimmune, chronic progressive non-suppurative inflammatory destruction of SMALL intrahepatic / intralobular bile ducts — not the large extrahepatic ducts. (Book p1020)

questions.sec: PBC: definition, AMA/PDHE2, hepatic vs cholestatic note, prevalence, associations, algorithm and presentation
questions.q: According to the printed definition, the destruction of small intrahepatic / intralobular bile ducts in PBC is mediated by which immune arm?
opts: T-cell only, with no antibody contribution
Both T-cell and B-cell, with T-cell predominating over B-cell
questions.exp: The arrow below the definition reads 'mediated by both T-cell > B-cell'. (Book p1020)

questions.sec: PBC: definition, AMA/PDHE2, hepatic vs cholestatic note, prevalence, associations, algorithm and presentation
questions.q: Antimitochondrial antibody (AMA) is printed as positive in what proportion of PBC patients?
questions.exp: 'Antimitochondrial Ab (AMA) 95%.' (ANA is the 50% antibody listed later on p1021.) (Book p1020)

questions.sec: PBC: definition, AMA/PDHE2, hepatic vs cholestatic note, prevalence, associations, algorithm and presentation
questions.q: Fill up: In PBC the antimitochondrial antibody is directed against ______.
questions.exp: 'Against : PDHE2.' The footnote to the Note table expands it: 'PDHE2 : Pyruvate dehydrogenase enzyme type-2'. (Book p1020)

questions.sec: PBC: definition, AMA/PDHE2, hepatic vs cholestatic note, prevalence, associations, algorithm and presentation
questions.q: Match each column of the Note table (Hepatic vs Cholestatic pattern) with its printed content — 1) Hepatic 2) Cholestatic … A) Fatigue and pruritus, progressing through complete destruction of bile duct to jaundice (poor prognosis) B) Jaundice as the predominant feature
questions.exp: Note table: Hepatic column = 'Jaundice (predominant feature)'; Cholestatic column = 'Fatigue & pruritus → complete destruction of bile duct → Jaundice (Poor prognosis)'. (Book p1020)

questions.sec: PBC: definition, AMA/PDHE2, hepatic vs cholestatic note, prevalence, associations, algorithm and presentation
questions.q: A patient with PBC who for years had only fatigue and pruritus now develops jaundice. Per the Note table's cholestatic column, what does this jaundice signify?
opts: Complete destruction of the bile ducts and a poor prognosis
Onset of the hepatic pattern, which carries the better prognosis
Transient viral superinfection unrelated to duct loss
Successful response to UDCA with ductular regeneration
questions.exp: In the cholestatic column the arrow runs fatigue & pruritus → 'Complete destruction of bile duct' → 'Jaundice (Poor prognosis)'. (Book p1020)

questions.sec: PBC: definition, AMA/PDHE2, hepatic vs cholestatic note, prevalence, associations, algorithm and presentation
questions.q: What female-to-male ratio and age band are printed under 'Prevalence' of PBC?
questions.exp: Prevalence: 'F > M = 9 : 1. 4th – 5th decade.' (Book p1020)

questions.sec: PBC: definition, AMA/PDHE2, hepatic vs cholestatic note, prevalence, associations, algorithm and presentation
questions.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the three disease associations listed for PBC on this page?
questions.exp: Disease association list: Sjogren syndrome with arthritis, Distal RTA (Type 1), Gallstones. Ulcerative colitis is the PSC association (p1021). (Book p1020)

questions.sec: PBC: definition, AMA/PDHE2, hepatic vs cholestatic note, prevalence, associations, algorithm and presentation
questions.q: Diagnostic algorithm: a patient with cholestasis undergoes ultrasound. Duct dilatation is ABSENT. What is the next printed step?
opts: Check AMA antibody; if positive, diagnose PBC
Proceed directly to liver transplant listing
Start empirical UDCA and reassess in 6 months
questions.exp: Algorithm: Patient with cholestasis → Ultrasound: look for duct dilatation → −ve → AMA Ab → +ve → PBC. (Book p1020)

questions.sec: PBC: definition, AMA/PDHE2, hepatic vs cholestatic note, prevalence, associations, algorithm and presentation
questions.q: In the same algorithm, ultrasound shows duct dilatation (+ve). What does the book direct?
opts: Perform liver biopsy for florid duct lesion
questions.exp: Ultrasound +ve for duct dilatation → 'Refer to surgery' (obstructive / extrahepatic cause). (Book p1020)

questions.sec: PBC: definition, AMA/PDHE2, hepatic vs cholestatic note, prevalence, associations, algorithm and presentation
questions.q: Presentation of PBC — judge: I Asymptomatic is the most common presentation. II Pruritus is the most common symptom.
questions.exp: 'Asymptomatic (m/c presentation)', 'Fatigue (m/c symptom)', then Pruritus as a separate bullet. (Book p1020)

questions.sec: PBC: definition, AMA/PDHE2, hepatic vs cholestatic note, prevalence, associations, algorithm and presentation
questions.q: Jaundice occurs in what percentage of PBC patients, and how is it characterised in the presentation list?
questions.exp: 'Jaundice (10%) : Late presentation (Poor prognosis).' (Book p1020)

questions.sec: PBC: definition, AMA/PDHE2, hepatic vs cholestatic note, prevalence, associations, algorithm and presentation
questions.q: Fill up the bracket exactly as printed beside hypercholesterolemia in the PBC presentation list: 'Hypercholesterolemia (Against : ______)'.
questions.exp: The bullet reads 'Hypercholesterolemia (Against : Dihydrolipoyl transacetylase)' — the printed bracket names the E2 (dihydrolipoyl transacetylase) component that AMA targets; it is the antibody target, not a mechanism of hypercholesterolaemia. (Book p1020)

questions.sec: PBC: definition, AMA/PDHE2, hepatic vs cholestatic note, prevalence, associations, algorithm and presentation
questions.q: Match the printed frequencies in the PBC presentation list — 1) Hepatomegaly 2) Splenomegaly 3) Jaundice … A) <15% B) 10% C) 30–40%
questions.exp: Hepatomegaly (30–40%), Splenomegaly (<15%), Jaundice (10%). (Book p1020)

questions.sec: PBC: definition, AMA/PDHE2, hepatic vs cholestatic note, prevalence, associations, algorithm and presentation
questions.q: Which of the following is NOT listed among the PBC presentation bullets on this page?
questions.exp: The list: asymptomatic, fatigue, pruritus, jaundice, hypercholesterolemia, xanthelasmas, hyperpigmentation, hepatomegaly, splenomegaly, steatorrhea. K-F rings belong to Wilson's disease. (Book p1020)

questions.sec: PBC: definition, AMA/PDHE2, hepatic vs cholestatic note, prevalence, associations, algorithm and presentation
questions.q: Steatorrhea in PBC is attributed on this page to which mechanism?
questions.exp: 'Steatorrhea (↓ Bile acid)'. (Book p1020)

questions.sec: PBC: definition, AMA/PDHE2, hepatic vs cholestatic note, prevalence, associations, algorithm and presentation
questions.q: The flowchart under steatorrhea lists three consequences of fat malabsorption and one downstream effect. Match — 1) Diarrhea 2) ↓ Fat soluble vitamin 3) ↓ Vitamin D absorption … A) leads to metabolic bone disease B) direct consequence of fat malabsorption (first arrow) C) direct consequence of fat malabsorption (second arrow)
questions.exp: Fat malabsorption → Diarrhea; → ↓ Fat soluble vitamin; → ↓ Vitamin D absorption → metabolic bone disease. (Book p1020)

questions.sec: PBC laboratory, histopathology, treatment; PSC definition, prevalence, HLA, presentation, UC association, labs
questions.q: Laboratory features of PBC — match the marker with its printed positivity — 1) AMA (Type IgM) 2) ANA … A) +ve in 50% B) +ve in 95%
questions.exp: Laboratory features: Raised ALP; AMA (Type IgM) +ve in 95%; ANA +ve in 50%. (Book p1021)

questions.sec: PBC laboratory, histopathology, treatment; PSC definition, prevalence, HLA, presentation, UC association, labs
questions.q: Fill up: The first laboratory feature listed for PBC is raised ______, and the AMA is printed as being of the ______ isotype.
questions.exp: 'Raised ALP.' and 'AMA (Type IgM) : +ve in 95%.' (Book p1021)

questions.sec: PBC laboratory, histopathology, treatment; PSC definition, prevalence, HLA, presentation, UC association, labs
questions.q: Which histopathological feature is labelled the EARLIEST change in PBC?
opts: Loss of the canal of Hering
Florid duct lesion with non-caseating granulomas
questions.exp: Histopathology tree: 'Loss of the canal of Hering : Earliest'. (Book p1021)

questions.sec: PBC laboratory, histopathology, treatment; PSC definition, prevalence, HLA, presentation, UC association, labs
questions.q: Which histopathological feature of PBC is labelled most common (m/c)?
opts: Loss of the canal of Hering
questions.exp: 'Ductopenia (m/c)'. (Book p1021)

questions.sec: PBC laboratory, histopathology, treatment; PSC definition, prevalence, HLA, presentation, UC association, labs
questions.q: Judge: I The most characteristic histological lesion of PBC is the florid duct lesion with granulomas. II These granulomas are caseating.
questions.exp: 'Florid duct lesion with granulomas (Non-caseating) (most characteristic)'. (Book p1021)

questions.sec: PBC laboratory, histopathology, treatment; PSC definition, prevalence, HLA, presentation, UC association, labs
questions.q: Match the PBC treatments with the printed descriptor — 1) Ursodeoxycholic acid (UDCA) 2) Obeticholic acid … A) Farnesoid receptor agonist B) ↓ progression of biliary cirrhosis
questions.exp: Treatment: UDCA : ↓ progression of biliary cirrhosis; Obeticholic acid : Farnesoid receptor agonist. (Book p1021)

questions.sec: PBC laboratory, histopathology, treatment; PSC definition, prevalence, HLA, presentation, UC association, labs
questions.q: Fill up (PSC definition): Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis is progressive ______ destruction of intra and extra hepatic bile duct, and is an ______ disease due to leaky gut.
questions.exp: 'Progressive fibrosing destruction of intra and extra hepatic bile duct. IgG4 disease d/t leaky gut.' (Book p1021)

questions.sec: PBC laboratory, histopathology, treatment; PSC definition, prevalence, HLA, presentation, UC association, labs
questions.q: Prevalence of PSC: sex predilection and decade printed?
questions.exp: 'M > F (2nd – 3rd decade).' (Book p1021)

questions.sec: PBC laboratory, histopathology, treatment; PSC definition, prevalence, HLA, presentation, UC association, labs
questions.q: Which HLA associations are printed for PSC?
questions.exp: 'HLA Association : HLA B-8, DR-3.' (Book p1021)

questions.sec: PBC laboratory, histopathology, treatment; PSC definition, prevalence, HLA, presentation, UC association, labs
questions.q: Which item is NOT among the four PSC presentation bullets on this page?
questions.exp: Presentation: Fatigue, Pruritis, Leaky gut, Cholestasis. (Book p1021)

questions.sec: PBC laboratory, histopathology, treatment; PSC definition, prevalence, HLA, presentation, UC association, labs
questions.q: Which cancer is printed under 'Association with cancer' for PSC?
questions.exp: 'Association with cancer : Cholangiocarcinoma.' (Colorectal carcinoma appears separately under the UC association.) (Book p1021)

questions.sec: PBC laboratory, histopathology, treatment; PSC definition, prevalence, HLA, presentation, UC association, labs
questions.q: Interpret the printed figures for the PSC–ulcerative colitis association: '(2/3rd / 5%)'.
opts: 2/3rd of PSC cases have UC; 5% of UC cases have PSC
2/3rd of UC cases have PSC; 5% of PSC cases have UC
2/3rd of PSC cases develop colorectal carcinoma; 5% die
Both figures refer to the lifetime cholangiocarcinoma risk
questions.exp: 'Ulcerative colitis (2/3rd / 5%) (2/3rd cases of PSC have UC & 5% cases of UC have PSC).' (Book p1021)

questions.sec: PBC laboratory, histopathology, treatment; PSC definition, prevalence, HLA, presentation, UC association, labs
questions.q: Regarding the UC that accompanies PSC, judge: I It is associated with atypical p-ANCA. II Its type is pancolitis with rectal sparing. III The only treatment is transplant.
opts: I true, II and III false
II true, I and III false
I, II and III all true
I and II true, III false
questions.exp: Sub-bullets under UC: Atypical P. ANCA association; Type: pancolitis with rectal sparing; A/w colorectal carcinoma; Only treatment: transplant. (Book p1021)

questions.sec: PBC laboratory, histopathology, treatment; PSC definition, prevalence, HLA, presentation, UC association, labs
questions.q: Fill up: The UC associated with PSC is 'A/w ______ carcinoma'.
questions.exp: 'A/w colorectal carcinoma.' (Book p1021)

questions.sec: PBC laboratory, histopathology, treatment; PSC definition, prevalence, HLA, presentation, UC association, labs
questions.q: Laboratory features of PSC — which of the following is printed as NEGATIVE?
opts: Both IgG4 and p-ANCA are printed negative
questions.exp: Laboratory features: IgG4 antibody; Atypical P. ANCA Ab; 'AMA Ab : −ve'. (Book p1021)

questions.sec: PSC radiology, histology, treatment; PBC vs PSC comparison table
questions.q: Which radiological investigation is marked the investigation of choice (IOC) for PSC?
questions.exp: 'MRCP (IOC)' with ERCP listed beneath; both point to 'Strictures/Ectasia'. (Book p1022)

questions.sec: PSC radiology, histology, treatment; PBC vs PSC comparison table
questions.q: Fill up: Both MRCP and ERCP in PSC demonstrate ______ / ______ of the bile ducts (image caption).
questions.exp: '→ Strictures/Ectasia' and the cholangiogram caption 'Strictures/Ectasia'. (Book p1022)

questions.sec: PSC radiology, histology, treatment; PBC vs PSC comparison table
questions.q: What histological feature is printed for PSC (and labelled in the micrograph)?
opts: Florid duct lesion with non-caseating granuloma
questions.exp: 'Histological Features : Concentric periductal onion skin fibrosis.' Micrograph caption: 'Concentric periductal fibrosis'. (Book p1022)

questions.sec: PSC radiology, histology, treatment; PBC vs PSC comparison table
questions.q: Treatment of PSC on this page is surgery — what recurrence figure is printed?
questions.exp: 'Treatment : Surgery (25% recurrence).' (Book p1022)

questions.sec: PSC radiology, histology, treatment; PBC vs PSC comparison table
questions.q: PBC vs PSC table, row 'Population incidence' — match — 1) PBC 2) PSC … A) Young male B) Perimenopausal females
questions.exp: Population incidence: PBC = Perimenopausal females; PSC = Young male. (Book p1022)

questions.sec: PSC radiology, histology, treatment; PBC vs PSC comparison table
questions.q: Rows 'Disease type' and 'HLA association' — match — 1) PBC 2) PSC … A) Autoimmune disease; HLA association absent B) Fibrosing disease; HLA association present
questions.exp: Disease type: PBC autoimmune, PSC fibrosing. HLA association: PBC absent, PSC present (B-8, DR-3). (Book p1022)

questions.sec: PSC radiology, histology, treatment; PBC vs PSC comparison table
questions.q: Row 'Smoking' — judge: I Smoking increases the risk of PBC. II Smoking is protective in PSC.
questions.exp: Smoking: PBC = Increase risk; PSC = Protective. (Book p1022)

questions.sec: PSC radiology, histology, treatment; PBC vs PSC comparison table
questions.q: Rows 'Disease association' and 'Diagnostic feature' — match — 1) PBC 2) PSC … A) Sjogren's syndrome; AMA Ab B) Ulcerative colitis; MRCP
questions.exp: Disease association: PBC Sjogren's, PSC UC. Diagnostic feature: PBC AMA Ab, PSC MRCP (printed 'IOP' in the table, 'IOC' on the same page above). (Book p1022)

questions.sec: PSC radiology, histology, treatment; PBC vs PSC comparison table
questions.q: A young man with ulcerative colitis has raised ALP; MRCP shows multifocal strictures and ectasia. Per the comparison table, what is the treatment listed for his condition?
questions.exp: The picture is PSC. Table row 'Treatment': PBC = UDCA; PSC = Transplant. (Book p1022)

questions.sec: PSC radiology, histology, treatment; PBC vs PSC comparison table
questions.q: Row 'Carcinoma association' — judge: I PBC is not premalignant. II PSC is associated with cholangiocarcinoma.
questions.exp: Carcinoma association: PBC = Not premalignant; PSC = A/w cholangiocarcinoma. (Book p1022)

questions.sec: PSC radiology, histology, treatment; PBC vs PSC comparison table
questions.q: Which of the following row pairings from the PBC vs PSC table is WRONGLY stated?
opts: Smoking: PBC protective, PSC increases risk
Population: PBC perimenopausal females, PSC young male
Diagnostic feature: PBC AMA Ab, PSC MRCP
questions.exp: The smoking row is reversed in this option: the book prints PBC = increase risk, PSC = protective. The other three pairings are correct. (Book p1022)

units.title: PBC — definition, AMA/PDHE2, patterns, prevalence, associations, diagnostic algorithm and presentation
units.guide: Cardinal intrahepatic cholestasis; autoimmune non-suppurative destruction of small intrahepatic/intralobular ducts, T-cell > B-cell; AMA 95% against PDHE2; hepatic (jaundice) vs cholestatic (fatigue & pruritus → duct destruction → jaundice, poor prognosis); F>M 9:1, 4th–5th decade; Sjogren with arthritis, distal RTA type 1, gallstones; ultrasound → AMA → PBC vs surgery; asymptomatic m/c presentation, fatigue m/c symptom, jaundice 10% late, hypercholesterolemia/xanthelasma, hyperpigmentation, hepatomegaly 30–40%, splenomegaly <15%, steatorrhea → fat malabsorption tree.

units.title: PBC labs, histology and treatment; PSC definition through laboratory features
units.guide: Raised ALP, AMA IgM 95%, ANA 50%; canal of Hering loss earliest, ductopenia m/c, florid duct lesion with non-caseating granulomas most characteristic; UDCA slows progression, obeticholic acid = farnesoid receptor agonist. PSC: fibrosing destruction of intra+extra hepatic ducts, IgG4 disease d/t leaky gut; M>F 2nd–3rd decade; HLA B-8, DR-3; fatigue, pruritus, leaky gut, cholestasis; cholangiocarcinoma; UC 2/3rd vs 5%, atypical p-ANCA, pancolitis with rectal sparing, colorectal carcinoma, transplant only; IgG4, atypical p-ANCA, AMA negative.

units.title: PSC imaging, histology, treatment and the PBC vs PSC table
units.guide: MRCP (IOC) / ERCP → strictures/ectasia; concentric periductal onion-skin fibrosis; surgery with 25% recurrence; table: perimenopausal female vs young male, autoimmune vs fibrosing, HLA absent vs present, smoking increases risk vs protective, Sjogren vs UC, AMA vs MRCP, UDCA vs transplant, not premalignant vs cholangiocarcinoma.
